newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO IN REPORTED $21.8 MILLION TRANSFER BID.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO IN REPORTED $21.8 MILLION TRANSFER BID.

text.p: Roberto Baggio, once the world's most expensive player, is ready to quit AC Milan in the hope of ensuring his place at next year's World Cup finals.
His agents are already sounding out clubs in England, Spain, the United States and Japan about their interest in the unsettled star, Gazzetta Dello Sport newspaper reported on Thursday.
The newspaper said Japanese club Kawasaki Verdi have offered a near world record transfer package of $21.8 million.
Baggio, 30 and in his second season with AC Milan, has made no secret of his unhappiness with the club, the defending champions but going through a troubled and unsuccessful season.
Although he started and scored in Sunday's 3-1 defeat by city rivals Internazionale, that was an exception to recent matches which have seen him playing as a second-half substitute, if used at all.

Gazzetta dello Sport said Baggio's agents had made tentative contact with Atletico Madrid and Real Madrid in Spain, Aston Villa in England, New York Metrostars and New England Revolution in the United States as well as Kawasaki Verdi.
Aston Villa's interest may be prompted by the Birmingham club's stock market share launch on Thursday which valued the club at around $208 million.
Since moving to Milan from Juventus at the end of the 1994-95 season, Baggio's career has gone into the doldrums.

Arguably the most famous Italian player of his generation, his status reached that of national hero following the 1994 World Cup finals where he scored five goals during Italy's run to the final, where they lost on penalties to Brazil.
Persistent injury problems meant Baggio missed much of both the 1994-95 championship winning season with Juventus and his first season with Milan the following year.
He is now fully fit again but appears blocked at Milan by coach Arrigo Sacchi, who took over the club in December following the resignation of Uruguayan Oscar Washington Tabarez.
As the Italian national coach, Sacchi picked Baggio only twice in the two seasons subsequent to USA 94, ommitting him from the squad for the Euro 96 finals in England.

Since his return to Milan, Sacchi has appeared to favour Marco Simone, Frenchman Christophe Dugarry or Montenegrin Dejan Savicevic rather than Baggio as an attacking partner for automatic first choice, Liberian George Weah.
Speaking last weekend, Baggio indicated he will leave Milan if Sacchi remains as coach next season.

"My wish is to stay at Milan, but only to play...Next season, I've got to play (regularly) in order to win my way into the France 98 World Cup side. I simply cannot sit on the bench all season as has happened this year.
"I think that Arrigo Sacchi has made his choices and...he doesn't believe in me".
AC Milan, 12th in serie A, have had a disastrous season and are expected to make sweeping changes after the season ends.
